top_choice_rationale: P001 credits the physiology of GLP-1 (Holst on proglucagon processing and insulinotropic action, Drucker on GLP-1 biology and receptor action) together with Mojsov for identification and synthesis of the active peptide. The discovery opened the field and is mature, with independently replicated outcome-trial benefit in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. The citation is narrow ('active form', not 'first'), so it does not rule on priority against others. P002 is a defensible second because the Drucker/Holst core is the same, but its development-centred anchor on Knudsen's acylation work is a step built on the physiology, and it would be a prize for a product step instead of the opening discovery. No award is clearly worse given the maturity of the achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Drucker, Holst, Mojsov or Knudsen, and my single-cell and brain atlas work is outside this field
